tldr: Canada's Real-Time Rail went live, with KOHO and Interac already announcing instant-payment support, and BMO listed a new TSX ETF. Elsewhere, fintechs kept adding yield, stocks, stablecoin and bill-splitting features that raise baseline customer expectations.
themes: Fintechs adding yield and investing to retain deposits
Social and everyday-payment UX (bill splitting, tap to pay)

highlights.headline: KOHO announces instant payments on Canada's Real-Time Rail, and Interac issues a statement on the rail's launch
highlights.why: A direct Canadian fintech rival is already marketing real-time payments to millions. Simplii needs a clear RTR timeline, since instant money movement will quickly become table stakes.

highlights.headline: Wise launches Wise Interest and Stocks for US customers
highlights.why: A money-transfer player is bundling interest and investing to hold customer deposits. This is the same hold-your-whole-balance playbook Wealthsimple and EQ Bank use, so it is worth watching for a Canadian rollout.

highlights.headline: BMO lists the Credit Stress Opportunities ETF (ZCDX) on the TSX
highlights.why: A direct competitor is expanding its niche ETF shelf. It is a reminder to review the range of products available to Simplii self-directed investors.

highlights.headline: Venmo adds receipt scanning to split bills by item, while SoFi launches a USD stablecoin and PNC rolls out Coinbase-powered stablecoin payments for corporate clients
highlights.why: Peer-to-peer splitting is getting smarter, and stablecoins are moving from crypto niche to bank and fintech infrastructure. Both set expectations for payments UX and future rails.
